The child was a two year old girl, well until about five days before death. She developed a high fever and began breathing very fast, with the lower part of her chest pulling in on each breath, and she had a cough. She would not eat or drink, became very hot to the touch, and grew drowsy and hard to wake. A clinic gave some medicine but she did not improve. Her breathing became faster and her lips looked blue at times. There was no diarrhea and no rash. There was no injury and no convulsions. On the last day she stopped feeding, her breathing became shallow, and she died at home in the early morning.

The child was an eighteen month old boy. About four days before he died he began passing many loose, watery stools, more than eight times a day, and vomited several times. He became very thirsty at first, then stopped drinking. His eyes looked sunken, his mouth was dry, and when the skin on his abdomen was pinched it went back slowly. He passed very little urine in the last day. The family gave him some home fluids but could not reach a clinic in time. He became weak and unresponsive and died at home. There was no fever noted and no cough.

The child was a nine day old newborn, born at home at term after a normal pregnancy. On the third day of life he began to feed poorly and felt hot. He became less active, his cry grew weak, and his hands and feet felt cold. On the day of death he had fast breathing and a brief episode of jerking of the arms and legs. His skin developed a yellow color. There was no report of injury. He was taken toward a health facility but died on the way. The mother had prolonged labor and the cord was cut with a home blade.

The child was a three year old boy living in a malaria-endemic rural area. He had high fever with chills for about three days, was very tired, and refused food. On the second day he became confused and then had repeated convulsions. His urine was noted to be dark. He grew pale and his breathing was deep and fast. He was carried to a clinic where he was given an injection, but he remained unconscious and died the following night. There was no cough and no diarrhea, and no history of injury.

The child was a four year old girl. She had a fever and sore throat for several days, then developed a barking cough and noisy, difficult breathing that grew worse at night. She drooled and could not swallow well, and her breathing became labored with indrawing of the chest and neck. Her lips turned bluish and she became restless and then very quiet. The family sought care but the facility was far. She stopped breathing at home. There was no diarrhea, no rash, and no reported injury or convulsions.

The child was a fifteen month old boy who had not received all his vaccinations. He developed a high fever, red watery eyes, a runny nose, and a harsh cough, and a few days later a blotchy red rash appeared on his face and spread down his body. He then developed fast, difficult breathing and became very weak, unable to feed. His mouth had white patches and he had some loose stools. He was taken to a clinic but died two days later. The rash was still visible at the time of death.

The child was a two year old boy. He had a high fever for two days and became increasingly irritable, then drowsy. He vomited repeatedly and cried when his neck was moved. On the day of death he had a convulsion and his body became stiff, then he lost consciousness. A small pinpoint rash was noted on his legs. There was no cough, no diarrhea, and no history of injury. He was rushed to a facility but died shortly after arrival.

The child was a thirty month old girl who had been slowly wasting for several months. She was very thin with visible ribs and loose skin over her buttocks, and her hair had turned pale and thin. She had poor appetite and occasional diarrhea. In the final week she became apathetic, cold, and stopped eating entirely. She developed a mild cough and fast breathing at the end. The family had little food at home. She died quietly at home. There was no rash and no convulsions.

The child was a five month old boy who had breathed and fed poorly since birth. His lips and fingertips often looked bluish, especially when crying, and he tired quickly during feeds and sweated heavily. He gained weight slowly and had frequent chest infections. In the last days his breathing became rapid and labored and his color worsened. A clinic had once said something was wrong with his heart. He died at home. There was no fever at the end, no diarrhea, and no injury.

The child was a three year old boy who was playing near an open water container while unsupervised. He was found face down in the water and pulled out unresponsive after a few minutes. The family tried to revive him and rushed him to a clinic, but he did not recover and was declared dead. He had been completely well before the event, with no fever, cough, diarrhea, rash, or prior illness. There was no other injury noted.
